draft.title: Derived and non-metric measures
card: Speed
is distance ÷ time. A car that travels 150 km in 2 hours has a speed of 150 ÷ 2 = 75 km/h.
Fuel use
is shown as litres per 100 km. If a car uses 8 L to go 100 km, it uses 8 ÷ 100 = 0.08 L for each km.
Flow rate
is volume ÷ time, such as litres per minute. A tap that fills 12 L in 3 minutes runs at 12 ÷ 3 = 4 L/min.
Inches
are still used in trades. 1 inch = 25.4 mm. To convert 3 inches to mm, multiply: 3 × 25.4 = 76.2 mm. To go from mm to inches, divide by 25.4.
draft.remember: Rates divide one measure by another. To change units, multiply or divide by the conversion number.

a.q: A tank pipe fills 90 L in 6 minutes. What is the flow rate?
a.why: Flow rate = 90 ÷ 6 = 15 L/min. Multiplying 90 × 6 = 540 is wrong because a rate divides volume by time.

b.q: A carpenter in Geelong needs a pipe 4 inches wide. What is this in mm?
b.why: Inches are larger than mm, so multiply: 4 × 25.4 = 101.6 mm. Dividing 25.4 by 4 gives 6.35, which is wrong because it uses the wrong operation.
b.clue: 1 inch is 25.4 mm, and a mm is smaller.

check.summary: No problems found. The card's facts and worked examples are correct (1 inch = 25.4 mm), and both questions have one clearly right answer (15 L/min and 101.6 mm) that matches the explanations.
